The Tamaulipas state prosecutor's office reports roughly 30 femicides recorded in the state so far in 2026, according to a Lado.mx report published Tuesday, October 20. One of the cases still under investigation: the murder of Keyla Salinas in Nuevo Laredo.

Salinas was killed on October 9 inside the shop where she worked selling Jafra products, on Morelos street in Nuevo Laredo's Sector Centro, according to Noticias en Contraste. The killing is being investigated as intentional homicide. Preliminary information points to a possible robbery as the motive — unofficial accounts say an intruder tried to take products from the shop and attacked her with a bladed weapon, leaving her wounded inside the establishment. How the attack unfolded and who is responsible have not been established; the case remains open.

Family and friends have posted messages mourning her and demanding justice. Salinas was a member of the Templo Centro de Restauración congregation in Nuevo Laredo.

What we're watching

  • Whether the state prosecutor's office formally classifies the Salinas case as femicide — and whether the robbery theory holds as the investigation advances.
  • Whether an arrest follows. As of Tuesday's reporting, no suspect has been publicly identified.
  • How the state's 2026 femicide count moves as the year closes — and what it takes for an investigation to become a charge, not just a statistic.

For families in Nuevo Laredo, the number that matters is not 30. It is one: the person who took Keyla Salinas's life has not been found.

Update — October 20, 2026

The state's femicide count has moved since this story was published — and not in a good direction. New figures from Mexico's National Public Security System (SESNSP) for January through September 2026, analyzed by TResearch, put Tamaulipas at 34 femicide victims this year, up from 29 through August. Tamaulipas now ranks third nationally in absolute numbers, behind Sinaloa (97) and the State of Mexico (39), and carries a rate of 2.4 victims per 100,000 women — more than double the national average. TResearch notes this is Tamaulipas's worst January-to-September start since 2015. On the Salinas case itself, there is no new official word: no suspect has been publicly identified and the killing is still being investigated as intentional homicide with a possible robbery motive.

Sources: Lado.mx, "Suman alrededor de 30 feminicidios en Tamaulipas; investigan crimen de Keyla en Nuevo Laredo," Oct. 20, 2026; Noticias en Contraste, "Asesinan a Keyla en local de Nuevo Laredo; investigan presunto robo," Oct. 9, 2026; TResearch, "Feminicidios en México: cifras oficiales (Sep/2026)," Oct. 2026, citing SESNSP.

title: Tamaulipas Counts Roughly 30 Femicides in 2026 as Keyla Salinas's Murder in Nuevo Laredo Remains Under Investigation
